Summary (auto): quick mid-week check to validate a few benchmark slices and confirm the on-prem test plan and tuning knobs for the pilot

00:00 Maya: hey team, quick agenda  - validate last week's p95 gains, confirm cold-start plan, and next steps for on-prem
00:10 Rachel: thanks maya, we want to make sure the p95 improvements are reproducible and understand the cold windows
00:18 Arjun: i'll start with a short walkthrough  - slide one is p50/p95 across the chat workload. baseline p50 ~85ms p95 ~220ms; redwood hosted with persistent kv and batch=8 p50 ~69ms p95 ~112ms
00:40 Daniel: is that measured with persistent cache mounted across restarts or just warmed?
00:46 Liam: for that row we had a persistent mount. we also did a cold-start experiment where cache wasn't mounted and p95 went up to ~275ms; details are in the csv
01:05 Rachel: can you highlight which part of the workload produced the most cache reuse? some prefixes are highly repeated
01:12 Arjun: sure  - most gains came from multi-turn prefixes and repeated system prompts; we measured ~72% prefix reuse on your sample set leading to a big tail improvement
01:28 Priya: micro question on quantization  - int8 vs q4 quality tradeoffs?
01:34 Arjun: int8 had near-zero regression on your golden set (<0.5% metric delta) and improved latency ~15% vs float; q4 pushed latency more but had a few edge-case failures we flagged in the 'q4-edgecases' folder
01:50 Rachel: we'll want to see the failing examples, please include context and why they fail
01:55 Liam: yes those are in the shared drive, example ids q4-fail-01..03, we included reference outputs and diff notes
02:06 Daniel: throughput numbers again  - tokens/sec and QPS at steady-state?
02:10 Arjun: with batch=8 int8 on vA100 equiv we saw aggregate ~2.4k tokens/sec and QPS ~40 for 4 concurrent clients; baseline was ~1.6k tokens/sec and QPS ~24 in the same harness
02:30 Priya: how sensitive is the QPS to batch size? if we drop to batch=4 to reduce single-request latency what happens to QPS and cost?
02:37 Liam: batch=4 reduced p50 by a few ms but QPS dropped ~10-12% and cost per token rose; we recommend adaptive batching policy that keeps small batch under light load and ramps under high load
02:55 Rachel: about cold starts  - last time redwood measured a 5min prewarm, can you do a true zero-cold run for on-prem too?
03:02 Arjun: yes we'll include a true zero-cold run and a 5min warm run in the on-prem plan
03:14 Daniel: for on-prem we'll run the tests but need the exact docker tag and driver/port list
03:20 Maya: we'll share the bundle and the driver matrix; arjun will attach notes on kernel builds and expected deltas
03:30 Priya: SOC2 and audit logs  - can we stream per-request logs to our SIEM? retention needed for audits
03:36 Liam: yes we emit per-request metadata, token counts, model variant and can forward audit stream to your SIEM; retention configurable and we will share SOC2 summary
03:48 Rachel: fallback policy  - we need fallback only to in-VPC pinned variants, not to cloud providers for PHI data
03:54 Liam: policy is configurable, pilot will lock fallback to pinned internal variants only
04:02 Daniel: scheduling jitter  - did you see noisy neighbor runs? we'll compare to our cluster metrics after you share raw logs
04:08 Arjun: we repeated runs 5x and flagged noisy runs; raw logs and per-run metrics will be uploaded
04:20 Rachel: timeline  - run on-prem week of 3/23, then reconvene the following week?
04:25 Maya: yes we'll aim to meet the week after the on-prem run to finalize recommendations, target 2026-03-31 for the final report
04:34 Priya: procurement note  - include 6-month TCO for dedicated and comparisons to baseline in the final doc
04:40 Maya: will include in the pilot pricing workbook
04:45 Rachel: thanks everyone, that covers it for me
04:48 Daniel: same here
04:50 Maya: great, action items will be uploaded and we'll follow up, thanks all
04:56 Priya: bye
04:58 Maya: bye
